name: TL5001CDR
title: TL5001, TL5001A: PWM controllers with error amplifier, dead-time control, UVLO and short-circuit protection
summary: A pulse-width-modulation controller for dc-to-dc converters, running from 3.6 V to 40 V with an oscillator set from 20 kHz to 500 kHz by one resistor. It holds a 1 V reference, an error amplifier, a dead-time input that limits the maximum duty cycle, undervoltage lockout, a latching short-circuit timer, and an open-collector output for driving an external switch. TL5001A parts hold the reference to ±3 % against ±5 % for TL5001. TL5001CDR is the C-grade TL5001 in the 8-pin SOIC on tape and reel.
key_figures: 20 kHz to 500 kHz (Rt 15 kΩ to 250 kΩ)
open collector, 50 V and 20 mA recommended; 51 V and 21 mA absolute
1.4 mA typ, 2.1 mA max at Rt = 100 kΩ
3 V upper, 2.8 V lower threshold typ at 25 °C
80 dB open loop, 1.5 MHz unity gain

notes: TL5001 parts hold the reference to ±5 %, TL5001A parts to ±3 %. The letter after TL5001 or TL5001A sets the temperature grade: C, I, Q or M. The package letters follow: D (8-pin SOIC), P (8-pin plastic DIP), PS (8-pin SO), JG (8-pin ceramic DIP), FK (20-terminal ceramic chip carrier). An R after the package letters means tape and reel; G4 and E4 are lead-finish variants of the same part.

Operating temperature grades in the electrical tables: C -20 °C to 85 °C, I -40 °C to 85 °C, Q -40 °C to 125 °C, M -55 °C to 125 °C. The ordering list gives -25 to 85 °C for the TL5001CD, TL5001CP and TL5001CPSR parts and their variants, -40 to 125 °C for TL5001CPS, TL5001IPSR and every part number ending in .A.
The 5962- numbers are the military (QML) order codes of the M-grade ceramic parts: 5962-9958301QPA is TL5001MJGB, 5962-9958302QPA is TL5001AMJGB, 5962-9958302Q2A is TL5001AMFKB.
Other qualified versions: automotive TL5001A-Q1; military TL5001M and TL5001AM.

circuits.title: Step-down converter, 5 V to 3.3 V
circuits.description: A 5 V to 3.3 V buck regulator switching at 200 kHz. U1's open-collector output pulls the gate of the P-channel MOSFET Q1 low to turn it on, and R1 pulls the gate back up to the input to turn it off. Q1, the Schottky diode CR1, L1 and C2 form the power stage. R5 and R6 divide the output down to the 1 V reference at FB; R4 and C6 from COMP to FB and R7 with C7 across R5 compensate the loop. R3 on RT sets the frequency, R2 on DTC limits the duty cycle to 90 %, and C5 across R2 gives a 5.6 ms soft-start time constant. C4 on SCP sets the short-circuit timer; C1 and C3 bypass the input and the VCC pin.

parts.note: CTX20-1, or 23 turns of #28 wire on a Micrometals T50-26B core

notes: Switching frequency 200 kHz.
Maximum duty cycle 90 %.
Soft-start time constant 5.6 ms.
SCP time constant 70 ms.
Q1 TPS1101 and U1 from Texas Instruments; C1 and C2 from AVX; L1 CTX20-1 from Coiltronics; CR1 MBRS140T3 from Motorola.

operation.text: One chip holds a complete PWM controller: a 2.5 V internal regulator and 1 V reference, an error amplifier, a triangle oscillator, a PWM comparator that also takes the dead-time input, undervoltage lockout, a latching short-circuit timer and an output transistor with an open collector. The error amplifier's common-mode range is 0 V to 1.5 V.

An internal 2.5 V regulator fed from VCC supplies the circuitry and sets the levels the error amplifier and the SCP circuit work against. A resistor divider takes 1 V from it for the error amplifier's positive input; across operating temperature that 1 V typically stays within 2 %.

The amplifier compares the divided-down converter output on FB with 1 V and drives COMP, which feeds the PWM comparator and is the node for loop compensation. COMP sources only 45 µA, so its total dc load is 100 kΩ or more.

A resistor from RT to GND sets the oscillator from 20 kHz to 500 kHz; usable values are 15 kΩ to 250 kΩ, and the frequency-against-timing-resistance curve gives the frequency for a given resistor. The oscillator is a triangle running from about 0.7 V to about 1.3 V. Whenever the triangle sits above the lower of COMP and DTC, the PWM comparator holds the output transistor off.

DTC limits the maximum duty cycle below 100 %, which boost and flyback converters need. DTC sources a current IDT nominally the same as the current drawn from RT, so a resistor from DTC to GND sets a voltage VDT. The maximum duty cycle is nominally 0 % with VDT at 0.7 V or below and 100 % at 1.3 V or above. Because the triangle amplitude changes with frequency and RT has a source impedance of about 1250 Ω, the resistor for a chosen maximum duty cycle uses the triangle limits at the operating frequency.

A capacitor CDT across the DTC resistor makes VDT rise exponentially at power-up, so the duty cycle opens up gradually. The output stays off until VDT reaches about 0.7 V. Either UVLO or SCP tripping discharges CDT.
When VCC falls too low to operate, about 3 V at 25 °C, the UVLO switches off the output transistor and clears the SCP latch. It has 200 mV of hysteresis against noise and chatter.

On a shorted output the error amplifier drives COMP up to raise the duty cycle. When COMP passes 1.5 V, SCP comparator 1 starts a timer: an internal 185 kΩ resistor charges the capacitor on SCP from about 185 mV toward 2.5 V. If COMP falls back below 1.5 V before the capacitor reaches 1 V, the converter carries on normally. If the fault lasts until the capacitor reaches 1 V, SCP comparator 2 sets a latch that holds the output transistor off. The latch clears when VCC drops far enough to trip UVLO, or when SCP is pulled to ground from outside.
The output is an open-collector NPN rated 21 mA and 51 V. It conducts only while the triangle is lower than DTC and lower than COMP, and neither UVLO nor SCP is active.

In normal running the output pulses as the triangle crosses COMP. During a brief fault COMP rises just past 1.5 V: SCP comparator 1 trips and the SCP capacitor begins to charge, but COMP falls back, the capacitor is discharged and switching goes on. During a lasting fault COMP climbs to its 2.3 V limit; after the SCP timing period the SCP voltage passes 1 V, SCP comparator 2 goes high and OUT stays high with the transistor off. VCC has risen past 3 V before any of this.
A divider R1 from the converter output to FB and R2 from FB to GND, with a compensation network from COMP to FB, sets the output voltage; GND is the divider's return.
